approachQuestion.prompt:
Closed Inspection Tours

Given a directed graph on vertices 0 through n-1, return every simple directed cycle of length at least two, once up to rotation. Represent a cycle without repeating its first vertex at the end, rotated to put its smallest vertex first. Reversing a cycle is a different answer if those directed edges also exist.

Examples:
n=3, outgoing=[[1],[2],[0]] -> [[0,1,2]].
n=2, outgoing=[[1],[0]] -> [[0,1]].
n=3, outgoing=[[1,2],[0,2],[0,1]] -> [[0,1],[0,2],[1,2],[0,1,2],[0,2,1]].

Constraints: 2 <= n <= 10; no self loops or repeated edges. Outgoing adjacency lists are supplied; graph need not be connected.

options.text: For each start s, extend only to unmarked vertices greater than s. When an edge closes back to s, copy the current path; do not recurse into s. Undo ordinary vertex marks on return.
options.feedback: Every cycle has exactly one minimum vertex. Restricting its other vertices to larger values selects that rotation, while separately exploring directed choices preserves both orientations.

options.text: After finding the first edge back to s, return from the entire current search call without checking other outgoing edges.
options.feedback: In the complete three-vertex example, a path [0,1] may close to 0 but also extend through 2 to form [0,1,2]; returning loses the longer cycle.

options.text: Emit only cycles whose second vertex is less than their last vertex.
options.feedback: This treats reversal as equivalent; it drops [0,2,1] in the complete three-vertex example even though orientations are distinct.

options.text: Start a simple-cycle search from every vertex without the greater-than-start restriction, rotate each completed cycle to its smallest vertex, and deduplicate with an ordered set.
options.feedback: This is correct but searches each cycle under multiple rotations; the minimum-vertex restriction avoids those redundant branches.

feedback.reason: Every cycle has exactly one minimum vertex. Restricting its other vertices to larger values selects that rotation, while separately exploring directed choices preserves both orientations.
details: For each start s in increasing order, mark s and search simple paths beginning there. Scan outgoing edges: an edge to s emits the current path if it has at least two vertices; recurse only to unmarked vertices greater than s, then undo. Continue exploring after emitting so longer cycles remain reachable.

Require every other cycle vertex to exceed start, making start the cycle's unique smallest ID. This removes rotational duplicates without suppressing different directed cycles. After emitting a return edge, continue exploring other outgoing choices.

complexityQuestion.prompt: Analyze `acm-b18-19-search` only. Let V count all recursive calls over all starts, E count all outgoing entries scanned in those calls, and R count copied vertex IDs. Allocate n membership flags once, clearing each start and path mark on return. Scan the n starts. Choose the tightest stated time and auxiliary-space pair. Count recursion and mutable working state; exclude supplied input and returned output storage, but include copying work in time. Primitive integer/index operations and preallocated-array updates cost constant time; dynamic appends are amortized constant time. No hashing is used unless explicitly stated.

options.text: O(n + V + E + R) time, O(n) auxiliary space
O(n+m+R) time, O(n) auxiliary space, with m the graph edge count
O(n + V + E + R) time, O(R) auxiliary space
O(n + V + R) time, O(n) auxiliary space

feedback.reason: Count start initialization, search calls, actual edge inspections, and result copies.
details: The initialization/start loop contributes n, calls V, actual edge inspections E, and result copies R. Edges to vertices below the start still cost an inspection.
Only n flags and one path/stack of at most n vertices are retained. Completed cycles belong to output.

Let V count all recursive calls over all starts, E count all outgoing entries scanned in those calls, and R count copied vertex IDs. Allocate n membership flags once, clearing each start and path mark on return. Scan the n starts.
“O(n+m+R) time, O(n) auxiliary space, with m the graph edge count”: An edge can be scanned for many different simple path prefixes.
“O(n + V + E + R) time, O(R) auxiliary space”: Output is excluded; working membership and recursion remain linear.
“O(n + V + R) time, O(n) auxiliary space”: Rejected outgoing edges still require inspection.
